source_snapshot.procedure: Use BMC WebUI to set Always power off, reboot BMC and verify persistence, then with SUT power on/off unplug and replug AC and inspect SUT power state.
source_snapshot.criteria: Policy does not change; Always power off makes the SUT remain off after AC returns.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL proposes setting/readback of Redfish PowerRestorePolicy=AlwaysOff and delegates AC removal/restoration to an operator, but omits exact system/resource discovery, original-policy recovery, both source starting states, complete multi-feed isolation, BMC-reboot persistence, observation windows and final OS recovery.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly treats the persistent write, BMC reboot and physical AC cycle as CRITICAL with staged approval, target/PDU mapping, workload drain, independent observation and original-policy restoration.

old_problem: The prior test design had a clear AlwaysOff objective but left safe execution details as Pending. API readback alone cannot prove behavior after true external power loss; pulling only one feed on a redundant system may not create AC loss; and failing to save/restore the original persistent policy can alter later boot behavior. These are bounded runbook and Project topology inputs rather than missing engineering semantics.
disposition_reason: DMTF standardizes ComputerSystem.PowerRestorePolicy=AlwaysOff as remaining powered off when external power is applied. The review can therefore define an auditable two-checkpoint case: persistence through a BMC-only reboot and behavior after actual loss/restoration of all approved AC feeds. The exact system URI, original policy, start-state matrix, feed/outlet map, timers and recovery remain Project execution prerequisites, while every policy write, BMC reboot and human AC operation requires explicit staged authorization.
decision_basis: XLSX row 979, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 980 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 980 / variant 1692245e76e444b5.

DMTF ComputerSystem defines PowerRestorePolicy AlwaysOff as the system remaining powered off when external power is applied, which supplies the authoritative policy value and expected behavior without OEM invention.

BMC reboot and external AC loss are different transitions: persistence must be checked after Manager/BMC recovery, while functional behavior requires independent proof that all feeds were actually removed and restored.

The source wording `power on/off` is preserved as two separately authorized initial-host-state subruns unless the Project authority formally narrows it. Each must retain its own baseline and AC event evidence.

ED-06, ED-08, ED-15, ED-17, ED-18, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve transition identity, actual WebUI/physical evidence, logs and recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 allow Project parameterization but require human physical action, staged confirmation and no automatic retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify AlwaysOff persistence through BMC reboot and true AC-loss restoration from approved On and Off pre-states
test_case.purpose: Verify the selected system's AlwaysOff power-restore policy is correctly set in the actual BMC WebUI/approved Redfish property, survives a BMC-only reboot, and for each Project-required initial host On/Off state causes the host to remain off after a human-controlled complete external AC loss and restoration, followed by safe policy and service recovery.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/ComputerSystem/Manager/firmware/WebUI identity and target-advertised writable PowerRestorePolicy property with AlwaysOff support
Original policy and owner-approved final policy/state, including whether temporary AlwaysOff must be restored after testing
Complete SUT PSU/feed/PDU/outlet/cable topology proving which operator-controlled feeds must be removed to create genuine external AC loss without affecting other equipment
Approved start-state matrix preserving both source On and Off cases or a documented owner ruling, with independent host power-state/BMC-ready/OS-ready observations
Maintenance window, workload drain/quiesce, console/recovery access, BMC reboot method, per-stage timeouts, AC-off dwell, post-restore observation window and expected event allowlist
Pinned reviewed Script, protected Redfish/WebUI access, actual rendered WebUI capture, human PDU/cord operator, observer, staged approvals and incident runbook
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Discover the exact ComputerSystem and confirm its advertised PowerRestorePolicy accepts AlwaysOff. Preserve original policy, current host/BMC state, workloads, alarms, SEL/audit logs and actual rendered WebUI value. After explicit policy-write approval, set AlwaysOff through the approved protected interface, verify response/readback and capture the WebUI. After a separate approval, perform only the approved BMC/Manager reboot—not host reboot, DC cycle or AC cycle—wait for full BMC readiness, rediscover resources and verify AlwaysOff persists. For each separately authorized source initial state (On and Off), establish and record that exact state; the On subrun requires workload drain and approval for abrupt AC loss. A human operator verifies the exact SUT/feed/outlet labels, removes every feed required for true AC loss for the approved dwell, records PDU/physical evidence, restores the same feeds, and observes the bounded interval. Verify BMC recovery and ComputerSystem PowerState remains Off with no host boot/OS-ready signal. Preserve expected/unexpected events without clearing. Under separate recovery approval, restore the original/final policy, manually power on if required, verify complete Off-to-On-to-OS Ready recovery and final healthy state. Never substitute BMC reboot, host reboot, DC off/on or one-feed interruption for the AC checkpoint; never automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: AlwaysOff is accepted, read back and visible in the actual WebUI, then remains AlwaysOff after the BMC-only reboot and full BMC recovery. In each approved initial On/Off subrun, complete external AC loss is independently proven, and after all feeds return the BMC recovers while the host remains Off throughout the approved observation window with no automatic boot. Expected AC/BMC events match the allowlist and no unexpected fault remains. The owner-approved final policy is restored, any required manual power-on completes through OS Ready, workloads/reachability recover and the final platform is healthy.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target/property discovery, original-policy capture, protected AlwaysOff set/readback, actual rendered WebUI evidence, persistence after a distinct BMC reboot, human proof of complete AC loss/restoration, separately evidenced required On and Off pre-states, host remaining Off for the full observation interval, log reconciliation and final policy/OS recovery. Redfish/WebUI readback alone, BMC reboot, host reboot, DC cycle, removing only one live-redundant feed or evidence borrowed from AlwaysOn/LastState cannot pass. Policy drift, incomplete AC loss, automatic host power-on, wrong target/outlet, unexpected events or failed recovery is FAIL. Missing runtime identity/topology/timers makes execution NOT READY, not Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: No policy write, BMC reboot, host-state change or AC action without separate explicit approval immediately before that stage and exact SUT/BMC/PDU/feed confirmation.
Physical AC removal/restoration is human-only; the agent must not operate PDU/cords or infer complete AC loss from one PSU on a redundant platform.
Drain/quiesce workloads and verify backup/console/recovery readiness before the On-state AC-loss subrun; never hot-pull an active production service.
Capture the original policy and a verified restoration path before changing it; actual WebUI and API readbacks must agree before proceeding.
Preserve pre/during/post SEL, audit, PDU and power-state evidence; do not clear logs or collapse expected AC events with unexpected faults.
Stop on wrong target/outlet, write/persistence error, lost recovery channel, unexpected power state/alarm or incomplete feed isolation; do not automatically retry any reboot or power cycle.
expected_evidence: Staged approvals, immutable SUT/BMC/System/Manager/PDU/feed identity, workload-safe baseline and start-state matrix
Original policy plus protected AlwaysOff write/readback, request/response metadata and actual rendered WebUI setting captures
BMC-only reboot timestamps, reachability/readiness milestones, resource rediscovery and post-reboot policy persistence
For each On/Off pre-state: operator/feed/outlet record, complete AC-off proof/dwell, AC-restore evidence and timestamped BMC/host power observations
Expected-versus-observed SEL/audit/PDU events and explicit proof the host did not boot during the AlwaysOff observation window
Restored final policy, manual Off-to-On-to-OS Ready recovery, final health/workload evidence and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: On any anomaly, stop further power actions and keep the exact feeds in the owner-defined safe state. Use the approved console/BMC/PDU incident path; do not improvise another cycle. Once stable and separately authorized, restore the captured original/final policy, manually power the host on if required, verify BMC plus OS Ready and services, preserve all logs, and escalate any failed recovery without automatic retry.

source_conflict.reason: The Master consistently specifies AlwaysOff persistence and off-after-AC behavior. `power on/off` expands the required pre-state matrix but does not contradict the policy objective.

blocked.reason: DMTF defines the policy and expected state; Project-specific property support, feed mapping, timing, maintenance and recovery are bounded prerequisites rather than missing core semantics.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Actual System/Manager/property support; original/final policy; On/Off pre-state matrix; complete PSU/feed/PDU/outlet map; workload/maintenance approvals; BMC/AC/observation timers; event allowlist; WebUI/Script/recovery runbook.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Defines ComputerSystem.PowerRestorePolicy and AlwaysOff as the system remaining powered off when power is applied, plus ComputerSystem power-state semantics.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Data Model Specification 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Provides normative PowerRestorePolicy enum meaning and schema-driven discovery; the target still must advertise support and writable behavior.

project_authority: The Project owner supplies the exact System/Manager endpoints, writable interface, start-state matrix, full AC feed topology, maintenance/timing/event rules and final policy/recovery. These bounded inputs complete a standard AlwaysOff test without further engineering design.
